subject.title: Feature Request: Add parseMode config for Telegram channels

question: Should Telegram expose a persistent channel/account text-delivery policy, and which safe values and precedence should it support alongside `richMessages` and per-message overrides?
rationale: The missing config is source-proven, but choosing the permanent API affects escaping, trusted content, fallbacks, inheritance, upgrade behavior, and several delivery funnels.

options.title: Narrow safe policy
options.body: Add inherited current-HTML versus plain-text delivery, preserve current behavior as the default, and define typed per-message precedence.

options.title: Full parse modes
options.body: Expose direct Telegram modes including MarkdownV2 or raw HTML with complete escaping, trust-boundary, fallback, documentation, and live-client proof.

options.title: Decline new config
options.body: Keep the existing rich-message and per-message controls, document them clearly, and address concrete formatter defects separately.

recommendation.title: Narrow safe policy
recommendation.body: Add inherited current-HTML versus plain-text delivery, preserve current behavior as the default, and define typed per-message precedence.

likelyOwner.reason: The HTML transition and repeated central Telegram/config history make this the strongest available decision-routing candidate.
